title: Almost everywhere divergence of double Fourier series along shrinking conical regions
summary: We study almost everywhere divergence of rectangular partial sums of double trigonometric Fourier series along variable regions concentrated near the diagonal. Fefferman's theorem shows that, in two variables, unrestricted rectangular summation is radically different from the one-dimensional Carleson-Hunt theory: there are continuous functions whose rectangular Fourier sums diverge everywhere. Bakhvalov proved that this phenomenon persists even when the indices are restricted to a fixed cone-shaped neighbourhood of the diagonal.
